intended_object: The ℤ-grading of the total module ⨁ₙ C(G, …, C(G, X)) of the shifted coinduced resolution of X: in degree n ≥ 0 it is the copy of the n-th term (with n+1 layers of functions on G) inside the direct sum, and it is 0 in negative degrees. This comes from the docstring and from the lemmas `gradedResolutionPiece_natCast` and `gradedResolutionPiece_of_neg`.
explanation:
The definition applies the library's general `CochainComplex.directSumPiece` to the resolution complex `resolutionModuleComplex X`. That general construction is `extendByZero (fun n ↦ range (DirectSum.lof R ℕ K.X n))`. In degree d ≥ 0 this gives the range of the d-th inclusion into the direct sum, and in degree d < 0 it gives ⊥. This is exactly the standard decomposition of a nonnegatively graded external direct sum into its homogeneous pieces, indexed by ℤ.

The library proves that these pieces form an internal direct sum (`isInternal_gradedResolutionPiece`), that they agree with the inclusion ranges in nonnegative degrees, and that they vanish in negative degrees. It also proves that the differential has degree 1 and the homotopy degree −1 with respect to this grading. All of this matches the docstring.

The general construction already exists in the library for any cochain complex of modules, and this definition only specializes it to one particular complex. A grading of one specific module is a specific object, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no ready-made ℤ-indexed homogeneous-piece family for this resolution, so there is no Mathlib counterpart to cite.
